atoms.text: Sydney is the capital of the state of New South Wales. It was founded in 1788, but the region was inhabited by Australian Aborigines for at least 30,000 years. The city is located on the east coast of Australia. With about 4.7 million inhabitants Sydney is Australia's biggest city and also the industrial, trade and financial centre of the country.

atoms.text: After 14 years of building, the Sydney Opera House was opened by the former queen of Australia, Elisabeth II in 1973. This landmark of Sydney was designed by Jørn Utzon, a Danish architect who eventually won the Pritzker Architecture Prize. The opera house contains five theatres offering space for 5,541 spectators. In total there are about 100 rooms including 60 fitting rooms, six bars, four restaurants and a cinema.

atoms.text: Sydney Harbour Bridge was opened in 1932 and connects the north and south shores of the harbour, Port Jackson. In 2007, it was added to the Australian National Heritage List since, next to the opera house, it is considered a landmark of Sydney. Because of its appearance, the 503-metre-long bridge is also called “The Coat Hanger” by the locals. It is possible to climb the 134-metre-high steel bridge to get a view over the beautiful harbour.

atoms.a: Sydney Harbour Bridge connects the east and west shores of Port Jackson.
Locals call the bridge a coat hanger because it looks like one.
You can reach the top of the bridge with a lift only.

atoms.text: One of the most famous beaches and surf spots in Australia is Bondi Beach. The word “bondi” is an Aboriginal term describing the noise of sea waves breaking on the beach. The beach is located about seven kilometres east of the city centre and is one kilometre long. Usually, the south end of the beach is reserved for surfboard riding. Coloured flags mark swimming areas.

atoms.text: The Royal Botanic Garden is the biggest of three botanical gardens in Sydney. It is open every day and entry is free. This scientific institution was opened in 1816 and is thus the oldest historic botanical institution in Australia. It consists of different areas such as the Palace Gardens, the Bennelong Precinct and the Lower and Middle Gardens. The Middle Garden is most closely cultivated and contains both native and exotic plants.
